question.problem:
Consider the equivalence relation $∼$ on $R,$ defined by $x∼y$ if $\operatorname{cos}⁡x=\operatorname{cos}⁡y.$ Which of the following are in the equivalence class $[0]?$

I. $2\pi $

II. $3\pi $

III. $\frac{\pi }{2}$
question.worked_solution:
The equivalence class $[0]$ consists of the elements that are equivalent to $0$ under the given equivalence relation. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}[0] & ={x\in R\,|\,x∼0} \\  & ={x\in R\,|\,\operatorname{cos}⁡x=\operatorname{cos}⁡0} \\  & ={x\in R\,|\,\operatorname{cos}⁡x=1} \\  & ={…,-4\pi ,-2\pi ,0,2\pi ,4\pi ,…}.\end{aligned}
$$

We see that $2\pi $ is in $[0],$ while $3\pi $ and $\frac{\pi }{2}$ are not.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only."
